1.explanation: This minimal React app mounts one example of Modal (and ComposedModal) alongside ComboBox, OverflowMenu, and CodeSnippet. In each case you are passing both `aria-label="..."` and `ariaLabel="..."` simultaneously. By opening your browser’s Inspector and examining the rendered HTML attributes on the dialog container, the combobox list, the overflow menu button, and the code snippet’s copy button, you’ll see which prop the component actually honors. This reproduces the inconsistent support for hyphenated vs. camel-cased ARIA props across Carbon React components.
1.bug_scenario:
When you render various Carbon React components (Modal/ComposedModal, ComboBox, OverflowMenu, CodeSnippet) and pass both the hyphenated prop (`aria-label`) and the camel-cased prop (`ariaLabel`), only one of them “sticks” on each component class. For example:  
• Modal only responds to `aria-label` (camel-cased `ariaLabel` is ignored).  
• ComboBox, OverflowMenu, CodeSnippet only respond to `ariaLabel` (their TypeScript/PropTypes still declare `ariaLabel`, so hyphen-cased `aria-label` is ignored).  
This inconsistency makes it impossible to rely on one single naming convention across all components.  

The reproduce scenario below renders each of these components side by side with both props applied so you can inspect the generated DOM and confirm which one works and which one doesn’t.
